[LCCO.7.3] Multiple `timeout` clauses on one call are independent. Each has
its own timer fact and sibling rule ([LCCO.7.2]) and fires at its own duration,
and a firing leaves the other clauses' timers in place. An author may declare
`timeout 5_s:` and `timeout 30_s:` on the same call to escalate.

When a call declares more than one `timeout` clause, a `timeout` firing must
not retract the call's capture fact ([LCCO.5.2]), so a late answer can still
join it. The capture ends by an `on` or `error` match ([LSCP.2.4.1]), by
supersedure ([LRST.4.1]) or at the end of its lifetime ([LCCO.5.3]). A later
clause's sibling reads its own timer and joins no capture ([LCCO.7.2]).
